newsitem.title: USA: Mid-America sees dilution after offering.
newsitem.headline: Mid-America sees dilution after offering.

text.p: Mid-America Apartment Communities Inc said on Monday that the common stock offering it completed in March affected its results by about $0.01 per share in funds from operations in the first quarter, and it expects further dilution in the second quarter as it waits to invest the proceeds in appropriate acquisitions.
The offering was for 2.3 million shares at $28.75 per share. Another $50 million in preferred stock was placed in October.

"We believe that we will have fully invested the proceeds of the common and the preferred offerings together with their associated debt by the end of 1997, and thus we anticipate that these acquisitions will be accretive in 1998," chief financial officer Simon Wadsworth said in a statement.

Based on projected borrowings for the balance of the 1997, Mid America said it expects that 1997 funds from operations will be decreased approximately $0.01 per share for every 1/4 percent increase in short term interest rates.
First-quarter same-store revenues rose 1.7 percent, and the company sees greater improvements for the rest of the year.
"We expect there to be some further short term dilution in the second quarter as we patiently seek optimum acquisition opportunities," Wadsworth said.

Wadsworth said the company is seeking higher investment returns to reflect the maturing of some markets and is proceeding more slowly in its investment program than initially anticipated, which is projected to cost it up to 2 cents per share in the second quarter.

The company said that at the end of the first quarter, $23 million, or 7.5 percent, of its total debt was floating rate, including $6 million outstanding on its $90 million unsecured line of credit. The average interest rate on its debt at March 31, 1997 was 7.95 percent.
